rollups.text: Craig Baker’s single-page portfolio project began on 2024-03-15 as a semantic, accessible, SEO-conscious HTML5, CSS3, and Bootstrap 5.3.0 site with About, Skills, Projects, and Contact sections. The plan included a responsive navbar, six-item gallery, validated contact form, and 1200×800 desktop target. The initial three-sprint estimate set Sprint 1 for 2024-04-01; by 2024-03-15 the deadline had moved to 2024-04-05 to allow more accessibility work. On 2024-04-10, Sprint 2 was underway with a 2024-04-20 deadline, focused on SEO and contact-form integration. By 2024-05-05, Craig was finalizing deployment and optimization ahead of a planned 2024-05-10 public launch. Elapsed time from initial planning to planned launch: 56 days.

Craig Baker’s contact-form implementation evolved from a basic HTML/CSS/JavaScript form with name, email, and message fields on 2024-03-15 to vanilla JavaScript validation using the HTML5 Constraint Validation API and a planned POST to /submit. On 2024-04-10, he explored Formspree instead of a Flask backend; a test POST returned HTTP 200 with 250 ms latency, but he later encountered CORS concerns, intermittent 500 errors, and a test suite that passed 95% of 50 runs. He sought reusable validation, error handling, and retries. On 2024-05-05, the form was still being refined, including a reported missing-CSRF-token block and questions about Flask-WTF. Elapsed time from initial form work to the later integration and reliability issues: 51 days.

Craig Baker repeatedly worked on accessibility for his portfolio. On 2024-03-15, he prepared semantic HTML and WCAG 2.1 AA review criteria, including heading structure, alt text, keyboard access, form labels, contrast, and visible focus. On 2024-04-10, he sought accessible Bootstrap modal behavior and debugged inconsistent focus trapping across Chrome 112, Firefox 110, and Edge 112; he also reviewed modal focus management and form validation. On 2024-05-05, he aimed for visible focus on all interactive elements, added a skip link, and continued troubleshooting focus visibility in dialogs. A peer review was planned for 2024-04-02, and another scheduled review focused on accessibility and API integration on 2024-04-15. Elapsed time from initial checklist to the later focus-visibility work: 51 days.

Craig Baker’s portfolio gallery grew from an initial six-item gallery planned on 2024-03-15 to an eight-card gallery discussed on 2024-04-10, then to 10 cards after two projects were added that day. The gallery repeatedly involved responsive Bootstrap layouts, project-detail modals, image-path 404 errors, accessibility, and deferred or lazy image loading. On 2024-04-10, Craig reported that opening a modal was delayed by 400 ms while its three images loaded synchronously; he explored lazy loading and a 350 ms initial-load reduction using lazysizes v5.3.2. By 2024-05-05, he still wanted lightweight lazy loading while keeping the bundle below 100 KB. Elapsed time between initial gallery planning and the later optimization work: 51 days.
rollups.topic: project gallery growth and image loading

rollups.text: Craig Baker aimed to make his portfolio load in under 1.5 seconds on 4G and keep images below 200 KB, a goal recorded on 2024-03-15. On 2024-04-10, he reported reducing gallery images from 300 KB to 180 KB with ImageOptim and improving 4G load time from 2.3 seconds to 1.4 seconds. On 2024-05-05, he reported reducing total page size from 1.8 MB to 1.2 MB with image compression and PostCSS minification, and reducing Time to Interactive from 3.5 seconds to 2.1 seconds by deferring noncritical JavaScript. He also reported reducing repeat load time from 1.2 seconds to 400 ms with Workbox caching. Elapsed time from initial performance targets to these reported optimizations: 51 days.

Craig Baker planned GitHub Pages deployment using GitHub Actions on 2024-04-10, specifying peaceiris/actions-gh-pages v2.4.1. By 2024-05-05, he reported the pipeline was set up and had 99.9% uptime, but was weighing GitHub Pages against Netlify before a planned 2024-05-10 launch. He chose Netlify on 2024-05-05, citing built-in SSL and easier DNS management, and asked about deployment and DNS configuration for craigbaker.dev. This marks a change from the earlier GitHub Pages deployment plan to Netlify. Elapsed time from the GitHub Pages workflow request to the stated Netlify choice: 25 days.

Reported portfolio performance and size changes: gallery images decreased from 300 KB to 180 KB and 4G load time from 2.3 seconds to 1.4 seconds on 2024-04-10; total page size decreased from 1.8 MB to 1.2 MB on 2024-05-05; Time to Interactive decreased from 3.5 seconds to 2.1 seconds on 2024-05-05; repeat load time decreased from 1.2 seconds to 400 milliseconds on 2024-05-05. These are four distinct reported metric improvements, across 2024-04-10 to 2024-05-05.

Craig Baker reported two code-size reductions on 2024-04-10 and 2024-05-05: gallery JavaScript went from 120 to 85 lines, a reduction of 35 lines; portfolio CSS went from 450 to 320 lines, a reduction of 130 lines. These are separately reported refactoring changes.

Frameworks, libraries, and development tools Craig Baker repeatedly used, evaluated, or asked about for his portfolio: HTML5 and CSS3 (2024-03-15); Bootstrap 5.3.0 (2024-03-15 onward); Sass 1.56.1 (considered 2024-03-15); Chrome DevTools v112 (2024-03-15 and 2024-05-05); Lighthouse v10 (2024-03-15; further testing planned 2024-05-05); ImageOptim (used by 2024-04-10); Formspree API v2 (explored 2024-04-10); lazysizes v5.3.2 (used or considered 2024-04-10 onward); PostCSS v8.4.21 (used 2024-05-05); Workbox v6.5.4 (used 2024-05-05); Cypress v12.3.0 (used for end-to-end tests 2024-05-05); and Sentry v7.3.0 (considered for error monitoring 2024-05-05).

Craig Baker’s portfolio hosting and analytics reports changed over time: on 2024-05-05, he reported a bounce rate consistently below 35%, after earlier stating a goal of keeping it below 40%. This is a reported improvement relative to the stated threshold, not a measured before-and-after bounce-rate value.
